# gritz

> gritz runs coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex in parallel, each in its own sandbox, driven by tasks and events.

Every page is also served as Markdown: take its URL, drop the trailing slash and append `.md`. The root page is `index.md`.

## Documentation sets

- [Complete documentation](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/1941/llms-full.txt): every page, concatenated
- [Abridged documentation](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/1941/llms-small.txt): every page, with non-essential content removed
- [Users](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/1941/_llms-txt/users.txt): using gritz and its integrations
- [Operators](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/1941/_llms-txt/operators.txt): deploying and running gritz

## Start here

- [Getting started](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/1941/getting-started.md): Sign in to gritz, pick an organisation, create a task in the Web UI, watch it run, send a follow-up instruction and archive it.
- [What is gritz?](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/1941/index.md): gritz runs coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex in sandboxes, driven by tasks and events.

## Concepts

- [Events and links](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/1941/concepts/events-and-links.md): How tasks link to pull requests, issues and other resources, how a subscribed link lets an event on that resource wake the task, and where events show up.
- [Namespaces](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/1941/concepts/namespaces.md): How a task's namespace scopes which routing rules see its subscriptions, so separate workflows on the same resource don't wake or suppress each other's tasks.
- [Organisations, members and API keys](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/1941/concepts/orgs-members-keys.md): How organisations own tasks, runners and rules, what members and the owner can do, and what API keys and task tokens can access.
- [Routing rules](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/1941/concepts/routing-rules.md): How an organisation's routing rules match events by type and conditions, why the first match wins, waking versus creating tasks, public rules, and testing rules with a test event.
- [Runners](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/1941/concepts/runners.md): Where a task runs, how runners connect to an organisation, choosing a runner for a task, and what happens when a runner is offline.
- [Schedules](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/1941/concepts/schedules.md): Create tasks on a cron schedule, in a timezone, and run a schedule's task on demand with run now.
- [Tasks](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/1941/concepts/tasks.md): What a task is, how instructions and events start its runs, the task statuses, restarting and cancelling, archiving and auto-archive, and the task log.
- [Workspaces](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/1941/concepts/workspaces.md): What a workspace gives a task (the image, repositories, agent and tools), how to pick one, and who defines them.

## Using gritz

- [Agent tools](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/1941/using/agent-tools.md): The gritz tools every agent gets (get_my_task, update_my_task, create_link, report and get_github_token), what gritz tells agents to do with them, and how to write instructions that use them.
- [CLI](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/1941/using/cli.md): Use the gritz CLI to create, list and update tasks, read a task's log, open a shell in its sandbox and get desktop notifications, and configure its server and API key.
- [Web UI](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/1941/using/web-ui.md): A tour of the gritz Web UI, the task list and task page, schedules, events and routing rules, workspaces, members, keys and settings.

## Integrations

- [Custom events](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/1941/integrations/custom-events.md): Send events from any system, such as an alerting tool or a deploy pipeline, to gritz so they create or wake up tasks.
- [GitHub](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/1941/integrations/github.md): Install the gritz GitHub App, link your GitHub account, and route pull request and issue events to tasks; the events gritz receives, the reactions it posts, and GitHub credentials for agents.
- [Jira](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/1941/integrations/jira.md): Connect Jira to gritz with the organisation's Atlassian webhook URL and secret, link your Atlassian account, and route Jira comments, labels and assignments to tasks.
- [MCP](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/1941/integrations/mcp.md): Connect Claude Code, Cursor or any MCP client to gritz, over HTTP with OAuth or locally with gritz mcp, to create and manage tasks; the tools it offers, and task notifications through Claude Code channels.

## Reference

- [CLI](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/1941/reference/cli.md): Every gritz subcommand and flag, with its environment variable and default.
- [Custom event envelope](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/1941/reference/custom-event-envelope.md): The request and response of POST /webhook/custom, with every field, its validation, authentication and status codes.
- [Event types](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/1941/reference/event-types.md): Every built-in GitHub and Jira event type, with its source and type, its label in the Web UI, and the attributes routing rule conditions can match.

## Operators

- [Backends](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/1941/operators/backends.md): The sandbox backends a runner can use, Docker and AWS Lambda MicroVMs, how each runs a task, and when to use which.
- [Debugging](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/1941/operators/debugging.md): Read a task's driver log, log raw agent output with verbose, open a shell in a task's sandbox, and find and clean up task containers.
- [Deployment](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/1941/operators/deployment.md): The published gritz server and runner images, running a runner as a Docker Compose service, and upgrading a deployment.
- [Operators overview](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/1941/operators/overview.md): The parts of a gritz deployment (server, runner, driver and sandbox), who talks to whom, what each needs to reach, and the data model.
- [Runner](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/1941/operators/runner.md): Run gritz runner on your own machine or server, with an API key, a workspaces.yaml and the driver binaries it copies into sandboxes.
- [Secrets](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/1941/operators/secrets.md): Declare credentials in a workspace's secrets map so gritz masks them in the task log it ships to the server, and what is masked where.
- [Server](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/1941/operators/server.md): Run gritz server with PostgreSQL, single sign-on, the GitHub App and Atlassian integrations, and the endpoints it serves.
- [workspaces.yaml](https://docs.gritz.dev/pr/1941/operators/workspaces-yaml.md): Reference for the runner's workspace config, the container, setup commands, agent, MCP servers, capabilities and secrets of each workspace, and ${env:} and ${sh:} expansion.
